- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile, model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period spikes (especially 20-30 day horizon) — adjust upward by 2–5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing mean reversion — if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral, forecast should begin to converge toward recent mean, not continue trending.
- Overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +0.33 to +1.00) often lead to over-forecasting in next 3–5 days — apply downward correction of 1–3% for 2–4 days post-spike.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 → +0.33), model tends to misread trend direction — use sentiment momentum as proxy for trend persistence, not absolute value.
